title: An LNS loop over districts

blocks.text: The same inspection week as before. `improve(jobs, hours, plan, free)` is now given: one LNS step that frees the jobs in `free`, keeps every other job as `plan` has it, and returns the best plan it finds. The planner wants a loop around it.

Write `lns(jobs, hours, start, rounds)`. `rounds` is a list of neighborhoods (sets of job names), used in order, one step each. Return a pair: the final plan (a set of job names) and a list of plan values, the start plan's value first and then the value after each round. A round whose step finds nothing better leaves the plan as it was: replace the current plan only when the step's plan is worth strictly more, so a plan of equal value never replaces it (the reference compares with `>`). Compute values as whole numbers, by summing the picked jobs' values, not from the float `objective_value`.
Each step solves the model of the previous practice with the rows that keep the jobs outside the neighborhood as they are:
Think about which plan "current" is in the second round. About eight lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from week_lns import Job, lns

# Six pump-station checks; 40 crew-hours in the week.
week = [Job("W1", "west", 45, 15), Job("W2", "west", 35, 10), Job("C1", "centre", 30, 10),
        Job("C2", "centre", 15, 5), Job("H1", "harbour", 40, 20), Job("H2", "harbour", 10, 5)]
start = {"W1", "C2", "H2"}
west, centre, harbour = {"W1", "W2"}, {"C1", "C2"}, {"H1", "H2"}

plan, history = lns(week, 40, start, [harbour, west, centre])
print("rounds harbour, west, centre -> history:", history)
print("final plan:", sorted(plan))
plan, history = lns(week, 40, start, [])
print("no rounds -> history:", history, "plan:", sorted(plan))

cases.says: the history starts at the start plan's value, has one entry per round, never falls and ends at the final plan's value
with no rounds, the start plan and its value come back
a round improves the plan the previous round left, so improvements in two districts add up

origin.section: LNS Frees Part of a Good Plan and Lets CP-SAT Rebuild It

concepts: an LNS loop starts each step from the best plan so far and keeps only improvements
